Superseded by #34097 and #34098. Finite durable per-Session history now provides reconciliation, while the process-wide live event stream provides wakeups. Keeping those concerns separate avoids the mixed durable/live ordering and replay semantics introduced here.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #29571: Conversation permanently stuck after a vision/image error — same symptom where a session becomes broken for all subsequent messages after a model rejects image input.
- #17205: Text-only models still receive image read attachments in prompt context — same root cause where a non-vision model (GLM) ends up with image content in the context.

I just realized OP, is describing a feature request form his perspective, from mine, this is a bug where the default behavior should be to have the originally selected model in the vendor modal persistent. why is this closed? here's how llama.cpp manages fine grained control: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions/21445

I'm seeing the same issue on **Linux** (v1.17.11, Electron 42.3.3), so this is cross-platform.

Full evidence gist: https://gist.github.com/RockingSisyphus/53ceef8127c47871d5b0493be9842450

**TL;DR: 3,840 out of 4,030 renderer.log lines are ResizeObserver errors (95.3%). Three crash dumps collected within 24 hours. The feedback loop is triggered by dock/composer resizing, no plugin needed.**

The cascade originates from three co-located `createResizeObserver` calls that fire simultaneously when the composer dock resizes:

1. `packages/app/src/pages/session/composer/session-composer-region-controller.ts:99` — calls `getBoundingClientRect()` in every observer callback, zero throttling
2. `packages/app/src/pages/session.tsx:1171` — fires `scheduleScrollState()` + `fill()` on content area resize
3. `packages/app/src/pages/session.tsx:1509` — fires `scrollToEnd()` + `scheduleScrollState()` + `fill()` on prompt dock height change

The feedback chain: dock resize → #1 fires → re-layout → #2 fires → content resize → #3 fires → more layout → back to #1. All within a single animation frame.

Peak burst: 20+ errors/second, sustained for ~30 seconds producing ~200 errors in one burst. Under load this freezes the renderer → Electron watchdog kills it → crash dump.

Crashpad pending dumps: 235 KB, 260 KB, 421 KB (Jun 26-27).

It is the same issue as [29571](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/29571). But the bug is deeper than GitHub Copilot or GLM. Harness issue.

I would like to work on this.

My proposed scope is a small TUI-only fix: add an explicit plain-text paste command/keybinding that reads clipboard text and inserts it directly into the prompt, bypassing the current local-file attachment detection path. I would leave the existing Ctrl+V behavior unchanged, and likely use a separate default such as Ctrl+Alt+V because Ctrl+Shift+V is intercepted inconsistently by terminals.

I would not change Desktop behavior in the same PR unless maintainers prefer that, since pasting actual file clipboard items as attachments appears to be separate from pasting a plain text path.

Thanks for the duplicate check. I think this is related to both, but distinct enough to track separately unless maintainers prefer folding it into #11439.

The distinction from #11439 is that this is **not** asking for general tag-based reasoning extraction from normal text like:

```text
content: "<think>hidden reasoning</think>visible answer"
```

In this repro the provider/proxy is already using the OpenAI-compatible native reasoning field for the reasoning text:

```text
delta.reasoning_content: "thinking"
```

The only malformed textual piece is a **standalone closing marker** emitted as a separate OpenAI Chat content chunk at the boundary between native reasoning and tool calls:

```text
delta.reasoning_content: "thinking"
delta.content: "</think>"
delta.tool_calls: [{ ... }]
finish_reason: "tool_calls"
```

So the proposed defensive handling is narrower than restoring the removed `extractReasoningMiddleware`: ignore or treat as a boundary only when a lone closing marker appears immediately after active `reasoning_content` and before `tool_calls`. It should not parse arbitrary `<think>...</think>` text in regular responses.

The code path I observed locally is:

1. `packages/llm/src/protocols/openai-chat.ts`
   - `delta.reasoning_content` emits `reasoning-delta`.
   - `delta.content` first closes reasoning and then emits `text-delta`.
   - `tool_calls` closes reasoning again and emits tool input/tool call events.

2. `packages/opencode/src/session/processor.ts`
   - `text-start` creates a normal text part.
   - `text-delta` appends the raw text to that part.
   - Therefore the standalone `</think>` becomes persisted assistant text.

3. `packages/opencode/src/session/message-v2.ts`
   - persisted text parts are replayed into future model messages as assistant text.
   - tool parts are also replayed, so the next request can contain both a stray assistant text part (`</think>`) and the tool call/result context.

That is where it overlaps with #19548: the bad text can be replayed into later prompts. But unlike #19548, the source is not generic stale progress text from an older turn; it is a synthetic closing marker from the current provider stream being persisted as ordinary assistant content.

A minimal regression assertion would be something like:

```ts
const body = sseEvents(
  { choices: [{ delta: { reasoning_content: "thinking" }, finish_reason: null }] },
  { choices: [{ delta: { content: "</think>" }, finish_reason: null }] },
  {
    choices: [
      {
        delta: {
          tool_calls: [
            {
              index: 0,
              id: "call_1",
              type: "function",
              function: { name: "lookup", arguments: "{\"query\":\"weather\"}" },
            },
          ],
        },
        finish_reason: null,
      },
    ],
  },
  { choices: [{ delta: {}, finish_reason: "tool_calls" }] },
)

const response = await generate(...)
expect(response.reasoning).toBe("thinking")
expect(response.text).toBe("")
expect(response.toolCalls).toHaveLength(1)
```

Adding an independent reproduction from headless / unattended usage.

Setup: a reasoning model behind an OpenAI-compatible provider, with `limit.output` set low in config. Per-step output was effectively capped, so turns that combined reasoning plus a large file write exhausted the output budget before a final text part was emitted.

Symptom: opencode returned no final assistant text for those turns. The turn had clearly done work (reasoning and tool calls), but it ended at the output ceiling with no committed final text, so a non-interactive caller has nothing to act on.

Evidence that the output cap is the trigger: turns that stayed under the output budget produced a final answer and succeeded; turns that hit the budget ceiling produced no final answer. Raising the configured output cap reduced the failures. This matches the root cause described here: the artificially low output cap plus no truncation detection or recovery.

Two things would each have prevented this, and they line up with what is already filed:

1. Honor the configured `limit.output` instead of the internal cap, tracked in #29363.
2. Auto-continue on `finish_reason: "length"` rather than ending the turn, tracked in #17471.

Sharing in case the repro detail helps prioritize. The impact is amplified for headless usage, where there is no human to type "continue," so a truncated turn becomes a hard failure rather than a pause.

+1 with a headless data point. In unattended usage (no interactive user), this is not just an annoyance, it becomes a hard failure: there is no one to type "continue," so a turn that stops at the output cap returns no final answer and the caller records the whole step as failed. Several of those in a row can abort an unattended run.

Repro: a reasoning model behind an OpenAI-compatible provider, with a low effective per-step output budget. Turns that stayed under the budget produced a final answer and succeeded; turns that hit the ceiling produced no final answer. Raising the output cap reduced the failures, which is consistent with `finish_reason: "length"` ending the turn early.

Auto-continue on `finish_reason: "length"` (paired with honoring `limit.output` per #29363) would make opencode usable as a backend for unattended runs. Happy to test a build if one lands.

Thanks for flagging. #16559 and this issue are related but distinct:

- **#16559** diagnoses the issue at the **config resolution layer**: `import.meta.resolve()` on Windows returns a raw filesystem path (`C:\Users\...`) instead of a `file://` URL, so the plugin spec stored in config is already malformed before display.
- **#34141** diagnoses the issue at the **display layer**: even when the spec IS a valid `file://` URL, `dialog-status.tsx` uses `path.split(/)` to extract the name, which breaks on Windows backslash paths produced by `fileURLToPath()`.

They are two independent bugs at different pipeline stages. Fixing #16559 would prevent raw paths from entering config, and fixing #34141 would robustly display names from valid `file://` URLs on Windows. Both should be fixed for full Windows compatibility.

Came across this while debugging a related problem: **parent session todo list never updates after a subagent finishes.**

My approach is different from what the issue title describes. Rather than giving subagents `todowrite` access (which would still write to the *child* session, not the parent), I added an auto-merge step inside `TaskTool.execute`: after a subagent completes, the parent session's todo items that match the subagent's `description` (fuzzy match) get automatically marked `completed`.

**Why not let subagents call todowrite?** Even with permission, `todowrite` writes to the subagent's own session. The parent session would still see stale todos. The merge happens at the platform level, so the LLM doesn't need to remember to call `todowrite` after `</task_result>`.

**Failure handling:** if the merge fails (DB error, etc.), the subagent output text gets a `[!] Automatic todo update failed …` note appended, so the parent agent can fall back to calling `todowrite` manually.
